19. Then Passion <term>Ragā</term>, the daughter of Mara, spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

Cutting through craving <term>taṇhā</term>, the recruiter of the crowds,
many beings will indeed walk <note>the editor notes a variant reading: cross over</note> <gloss>the spiritual path</gloss>.
Indeed, this homeless one <note>referring to the Buddha</note> will pull many people away,
snatching them across to the far shore, beyond the King of Death.

20. <note>The Buddha replies:</note>
Great heroes, the <term>Tathāgatas</term> <gloss>Those who have thus gone</gloss>, lead indeed by the true Dhamma.
When beings are being led by the Dhamma, what envy can there be in those who truly understand?

21. Then Craving <term>Taṇhā</term>, Discontent <term>Arati</term>, and Passion <term>Ragā</term>, the daughters of Mara, approached Mara the Evil One.

22. Mara the Evil One saw Craving, Discontent, and Passion, his daughters, coming from afar. Seeing them, he addressed them in verses:

Fools! You try to crush a mountain with the stalks of water lilies.
You dig into a mountain with your fingernails. You chew iron with your teeth.
As if lifting a rock with your head, you seek a foothold in the abyss.
As if attacking a tree stump with your chest, you go away frustrated by Gotama.

23. Blazing with beauty they came: Craving, Discontent, and Passion.
The Teacher swept them away right there, like the wind blows away a fallen tuft of cotton.

->The Third Chapter<-

->Its Summary Table<-

The Many <term>Sambahulā</term>, Samiddhi, Godhika, the Seven Years, and the Daughters; this Mara-pentad was taught by the Buddha-Teacher. The Connected Discourses of Mara <term>Māra-saṃyutta</term> are complete.

<summary>The daughters of Mara admit their failure to tempt the Buddha, leading Mara to mock their foolishness before the chapter concludes with a summary of the section's contents.</summary>
